## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-blind: "This journal follows a double-blind reviewing procedure" and the author remains anonymous to reviewers; the author must anonymise the manuscript and any files, submit a separate title page, and avoid self-identifying citations (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines and https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/aims-and-scope, retrieved 2026-11-23). A guest editor who authors an article in their own special issue does not handle its peer review. Survey respondents report an average of 1.8 reviewers (n=29 record) and 1.0 (n=76 record) per submission |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Survey respondents: for the n=29 record, 17 later verdicts (15 acceptances, 2 rejections); for the n=76 record, 29 later verdicts (28 acceptances, 1 rejection) (https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/772 ; https://apasurvey.philx.org/journals/21680, all years, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source found |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, in the journal's submission guidelines: large language models do not satisfy authorship criteria; use of an LLM should be documented in the Methods section (or a suitable alternative part); "AI assisted copy editing" for readability and style does not need to be declared, and human accountability for the final text is required (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with documentation |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with disclosure of substantive use; copy-editing exemption). The publisher-wide page is stricter: it says even low-risk uses (language editing, formatting, translation) need a clear description of the use, so the two pages differ and the journal text and the publisher text should both be checked |
| **Summary** | Journal text: LLMs cannot be authors; document LLM use in Methods; no declaration for AI-assisted copy editing. Publisher text: AI cannot be listed as an author; all uses need a description and accountability statement; AI-generated or AI-assisted visual content needs an AI Declaration naming system, purpose and extent; prohibited uses include writing results or discussion independently, generating scientific claims or interpretations and producing data presented as empirical. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines and https://www.springernature.com/gp/policies/editorial-policies/ai-manuscript-preparation |

## Format

> Source: the journal's submission guidelines, live page https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23. The page says it is being revised after a change of submission system, so the title-page and statement instructions may differ in the submission interface.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Per the aims page: special issues or collections, topical papers, state-of-the-art surveys, topical symposia, short discussion notes and Author-Meets-Critics symposia, in English. OpenAlex type counts for 2021-2026: 695 articles, 31 book reviews, 17 errata, 9 editorials |
| **Word limit** | Stated as pages, not words: "The general length of our papers are 20 pages, double spaced (including references, footnotes, tables and figures). Exceptions may be made for larger submissions." Measured: median published article length 16 pages (quartiles 11 to 20) over 705 of 760 Crossref records with a parseable page range (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0048-3893/works) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Exceptions may be made for larger submissions (same page); no criteria stated |
| **Abstract limit** | An abstract of 150 to 250 words and 4 to 6 keywords. Measured: abstract median 153 words (quartiles 119 to 193, maximum 354); 20 of 290 abstracts exceed 250 words (Crossref and OpenAlex, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Reference limit** | None separate; references count within the 20 pages |
| **Supplementary material** | A section on Supplementary Information exists in the guidelines; limits not read |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found; tables are to use the word processor's table function and figures follow the publisher's artwork rules (same page) |
| **Style / submission format** | Word (docx) or, for mathematical content, LaTeX; plain 10-point Times; decimal headings of at most three levels; footnotes, not endnotes; author-date citations in parentheses, reference lists encouraged to follow APA 7 author-count rules; editable source files required at every submission; Declarations (funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data availability, authors' contributions) on the title page or in the submission interface; a data availability statement is required for original research |

### Orientation

> Counts below: Crossref journal-article records of this journal published 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (760 records), with abstracts merged from Crossref and, where Crossref had none, from OpenAlex (290 records have an abstract: 38%; by year the share ranges from 28% to 50%). A record is counted when the regex matches its title or abstract. Percentages use 290 as the denominator; counts are therefore lower bounds and the shares describe the sample that has abstracts. Title-only counts over all 760 records are given where they add information. Regexes are word-boundary patterns written in the tables. Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Theoretical. "argue", "defend", "thesis" or "objection" appear in 193 of 290 abstracts (66.6%; regex `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*`). The 2 abstracts matching participants or vignette terms were read: one reports a participant study of a humanities-based programme (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11406-026-00978-2) and one is a clinical-vignette reading of an ancient text |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Rare. Of the 3 "quantitative/statistical" and 5 "qualitative/interview" regex hits, the hits read show one mixed-method participant study (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11406-026-00978-2) and one qualitative corpus study (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11406-024-00793-7); the rest are philosophical uses of the words |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Moderate. The aims page welcomes traditional areas (normative ethics, meta-ethics, epistemology, aesthetics, political philosophy, philosophy of science, philosophy of language, metaphysics, philosophy of mind) and encourages applied philosophy of language, environmental philosophy, philosophy of technology and work advancing the Sustainable Development Goals. Counts: philosophy of science and physics terms 14.1% (41 of 290), cognitive-science and neuroscience terms 8.3% (24), animals, climate and environment terms 7.2% (21), aesthetics, art and fiction 4.8% (14), AI terms 1.0% (3) |

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

> Evidence layers: Crossref and OpenAlex keyword counts over 290 abstracts and title-only counts over 760 records (regexes in the cells); OpenAlex author-country counts over 758 works; the journal's aims text (live page). Retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | The aims page states the journal "is global in scope, submissions, and readership" and welcomes submissions "from perspectives that are under-represented in the field" (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/aims-and-scope). Author countries of the 758 works in 2021-2026 (OpenAlex works with at least one author in the country; a work can count in several): United States 213, United Kingdom 82, China 53, Poland 43, Italy 37, Germany 33, Canada 28, Australia 21, Spain 17, Sweden 17, Netherlands 15, South Africa 13, Brazil 12, Switzerland 12 (https://api.openalex.org/works, group_by authorships.countries) |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Present but small. The pattern `\bdecoloni\w*\|\bIndigenous\b\|\bBuddhis\w*\|\bConfuci\w*\|\bDaoi\w*\|\bTaoi\w*\|\bAfrican philosoph\w*\|\bIslamic\b\|\bIndian\b\|\bChinese\b` matches 9 of 290 abstracts (3.1%) and 10 of 760 titles. A progressive-Confucianism paper is among the latest articles on the home page (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406) |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Present. Feminist, gender or race terms (`\bfeminis\w*\|\bgender\w*\|\bracial\w*\|\brace\b\|\bracis\w*\|\boppress\w*`) 10 of 290 abstracts (3.4%) and 10 of 760 titles; the aims page invites "under-represented" perspectives (not defined). No other editorial statement on these topics found |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Mixed analytic, by topic mix: ethics and normative terms 33.1% (96 of 290), epistemology and belief terms 22.1% (64), metaphysics and ontology 16.9% (49), philosophy of science and physics 14.1% (41), free will, personal identity and responsibility 13.4% (39), mind and consciousness 12.4% (36), political and justice terms 8.3% (24). Phenomenology and continental names (`\bphenomenolog\w*\|\bHeidegger\b\|\bHusserl\b\|\bFoucault\b\|\bDerrida\b\|\bcritical theory\b\|\bMerleau-Ponty\b`) 3.4% (10). Named historical figures 7.2% (21). The aims page lists past contributors from analytic and logical traditions and says contributions "must adhere to high standards of clarity and argumentation"; no political position is stated on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Scope statement from the journal: submissions "should be broadly accessible scholarly contributions on topics of current or emerging philosophical interest, and must adhere to high standards of clarity and argumentation" (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/aims-and-scope, retrieved 2026-11-23). No required theoretical framing is stated.
- **What kind of engagement?** Accessible work on current or emerging topics; the page welcomes work advancing the Sustainable Development Goals as one emerging area. Observed practice: 193 of 290 abstracts (66.6%) use argue, defend, thesis or objection language (Crossref and OpenAlex).
- **Article type and length**: the general length is 20 double-spaced pages including references, footnotes, tables and figures, with exceptions possible, and an abstract of 150 to 250 words (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines). Observed median 16 pages (quartiles 11 and 20; https://api.crossref.org/journals/0048-3893/works).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: the home page lists open calls on "Philosophy and Contemporary Art" and a standing "Book Symposium" call (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No page read states what happens to out-of-scope submissions; the guidelines say submissions lacking the required declarations "will be returned as incomplete".

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref journal-article records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23, with abstracts merged from Crossref and OpenAlex, over the 290 records with an abstract (38% of 760). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Where I read the hits and part were not uses of the method, the score is set from the hits read and the row says so. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 1 | Regex `\bparticipants\b\|\bsurvey\w*\|\bvignette\w*` 2 of 290 (0.7%); of these 1 is a participant study (https://doi.org/10.1007/s11406-026-00978-2). The 3 "quantitative/statistical" hits were read: one is that same study, the others philosophical uses |
| Qualitative interviews | 1 | Regex `\bqualitative\b\|\binterview\w*\|\bethnograph\w*\|\bthematic analysis\b` 5 of 290 (1.7%); of 5 hits read, 2 are genuine qualitative work (a corpus study, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11406-024-00793-7, and the programme evaluation above), 3 are philosophical uses |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Regex `\bautoethnograph\w*\|\bethnograph\w*` 0 of 290 |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | `\bargue\w*\|\bdefend\w*\|\bthesis\b\|\bobjection\w*` 193 of 290 (66.6%); `\bconceptual\w*\|\banalysis of\b\|\baccount of\b\|\btheory of\b` 97 (33.4%) |
| Formal / logical proof (added row) | 2 | `\btheorem\w*\|\bprove[sd]?\b\|\bproof\w*\|\bformal (?:model\|framework\|semantics\|system)\w*\|\bmodel-theor\w*\|\baxiom\w*` 13 of 290 (4.5%); the broader logic/formal pattern 22 (7.6%) |
| Mixed methods | 1 | `\bmixed[- ]method\w*` 0 of 290; the programme evaluation read above combines quantitative and qualitative data |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 0 | `\bsystematic review\w*\|\bmeta-analys\w*\|\bscoping review\w*` 0 of 290 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The guidelines list "Ethics approval" and "Consent" among the Declarations authors must supply, and say submissions that omit relevant declarations "will be returned as incomplete" (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines, retrieved 2026-11-23). Participant studies are rare (1 read, Methodological Preferences), so the rule is rarely engaged |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are the norm: 688 of 760 Crossref records (90.5%), 2021-2026 (https://api.crossref.org/journals/0048-3893/works) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | The guidelines state that for authors who are "(temporarily) unaffiliated" the system captures only city and country of residence (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines). That is a handling rule, not evidence on acceptance odds |
| **Data transparency requirement** | A data availability statement is required for all original research; sharing is strongly encouraged, and the statement may explain access conditions where sharing is not possible (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-blind with a separate title page, and an instruction to avoid self-identifying citations (guidelines). Springer Nature allows preprints at any time (https://www.springer.com/gp/editorial-policies/preprint-sharing), but whether a preprint affects this journal's anonymity is not stated |
| **AI use** | Document LLM use in Methods; AI cannot be an author; copy editing exempt in the journal text, stricter on the publisher page (see AI Policy) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid; APC GBP 2390 / USD 3290 / EUR 2690 (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/how-to-publish-with-us); 294 of 760 articles carry a Creative Commons licence URL in Crossref |
| **Originality** | Submission implies the work is unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere, and the guidelines warn against salami-slicing (https://link.springer.com/journal/11406/submission-guidelines) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: the general length is 20 double-spaced pages including references, footnotes, tables and figures; exceptions may be made (Format). A manuscript far above that departs from the stated norm.
- **Anonymisation**: double-blind review requires an anonymised manuscript, a separate title page and avoidance of self-identifying citations (Peer Review, Format).
- **Declarations**: submissions without the relevant declarations (funding, competing interests, ethics approval, consent, data availability, contributions) are returned as incomplete, and original research needs a data availability statement (Format, Practical Concerns).
- **Originality**: the work must be unpublished and not under consideration elsewhere (Practical Concerns).
- **AI use**: LLM use must be documented in Methods; AI cannot be an author; the publisher page sets stricter description rules than the journal text (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher reports a 15-day median to first decision (Review Cycle Time), while survey respondents average 3.2 to 4.4 months to a response (self-selected samples); both are recorded and they conflict.
- **Competition**: no acceptance rate is published on the pages read (Metrics); survey initial verdicts are mostly rejections or revise-and-resubmit (Metrics).
- **Open access cost**: gold access carries an APC of GBP 2390 / USD 3290 / EUR 2690 (Open Access); the accepted-manuscript embargo length was not found.
- **Reformatting**: the page says the submission system recently changed and the guidelines are being revised, so title-page and statement handling may differ from the text (Format).

### Best Suited For

- Accessible, argument-driven philosophy on traditional areas: 66.6% of measured abstracts use argue, defend, thesis or objection language; ethics (33.1%), epistemology (22.1%) and metaphysics (16.9%) are the largest topic groups (Orientation, Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Work from outside the usual centres: the aims page invites submissions from under-represented perspectives, the board spans 13 countries, and the 2021-2026 author countries include China 53, Poland 43 and Italy 37 (Epistemological, Reviewer Pool Characteristics).
- Applied or emerging areas the aims page names: environmental philosophy, philosophy of technology and Sustainable Development Goal work (Framing Requirements); animals, climate and environment terms 6.9% (Sensitive Topics).
- Single-authored papers of moderate length: 90.5% single-author, median 16 pages (Voice & Style).
- Authors without a university affiliation: the guidelines state how unaffiliated authors are recorded (Practical Concerns); this says nothing about acceptance odds.

### Not Recommended For

- Participant-based or qualitative empirical studies: 1 participant study found among 290 measured abstracts (Methodological Preferences). The count shows rarity, not rejection.
- Highly technical formal work: formal-proof terms 4.5% and probability and decision-theory terms 0.3% (Methodological Preferences, Epistemological). A frequency, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a published acceptance rate or verified turnaround before choosing: the journal's pages give only a 15-day median with no definition, and survey figures conflict with it (Metrics, Review Cycle Time).
